title: Adaptive Slot Sidebar & Predictive Route Matrix for Workspace Switching
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Replace the monolithic, static left rail with a compact, context-aware 'slot' sidebar that promotes faster workspace switching, surface rollout states and cost lenses, and reduce cognitive load for power and occasional users. This ticket captures the current prototype, research findings, key interaction patterns, and handoff assets for engineering and PM.

Problem statement: Our current sidebar is long and topology-heavy: users spend multiple clicks and context switches to move between workspaces, open rollout views, or inspect per-route cost breakdowns. Power users open the command palette frequently; occasional users get lost in nested workspace lists. We need an IA and navigation model that: a) surfaces likely destinations quickly, b) makes rollout and cost state visible without extra navigation, and c) gracefully degrades for small viewports.

Proposed solution (high level):
- Slot Sidebar: a vertical stack of 'slots' (compact containers) that can adapt their contents by workspace, role, and telemetry. Slots types include: Workspace Chip (primary), Recent Routes, Saved Dashboards, Rollout Shortcuts, and Cost Lenses. Each slot is a self-contained surface that can expand into a transient flyout for quick actions (e.g., switch, pin, view details) without leaving the current page.
- Predictive Route Matrix: a client-side model that ranks candidate routes (workspaces, dashboards, model endpoints, rollout pages) by recency, frequency, role, and SLA alerts. The matrix powers two affordances: (1) prioritization of quick-access slots, (2) inline suggestions in the command palette with pinned contextual shortcuts.
- Rollout & Cost badges: Small micro-visuals attached to slot chips indicate rollout stage (canary, staged, full) and a cost lens icon that opens a micro-dashboard showing 24h token cost, latency distribution, and change since last deployment.
- Accessibility & keyboard-first: All slots are keyboard navigable (tab/arrow), with 1-2 letter quick-jump shortcuts. Command palette integrates predictive suggestions and can trigger slot expansion with Enter.

Prototype assets: High-fidelity Figma frames, interactive prototype flows for desktop/tablet, and a lightweight HTML/CSS reference used for early dev perf experiments. Links provided below.

Design rationale and constraints:
- Preference transparency: Users should always be able to see where they are and where they can go. We chose slot cards over purely iconified rails to keep affordances discoverable for new users.
- Minimal vertical footprint: Slot compression uses density-aware rules: show 3 slots on small viewports, 5 on medium, full on desktop. Overflow is handled with an adaptive "More" slot rather than truncating content.
- Telemetry privacy: Predictive ranking uses on-device/session metrics; server-side hints are optional and require opt-in per privacy guidance (see links).

Outcomes to validate in next two weeks:
- 20% reduction in mean time-to-switch (measured by telemetry on beta group).
- 15% fewer command-palette invocations for workspace switchers among power users.
- No regressions on keyboard navigation and screen reader announcements.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Slot sidebar implemented as vertical slot container with at least Workspace, Recent Routes, and Rollouts slots. 2) Predictive ranking endpoint or client model integrated and returning a ranked list for the active user. 3) Rollout & cost badges visible on slot chips and open a micro-dashboard flyout showing last 24h token cost and latency. 4) Keyboard navigation: focus ring, arrow key movement, Enter to open slot, Esc to close. 5) Accessibility: screen reader announces slot type and state; contrast meets AA. 6) Small-view behavior: slots compress to 3 visible items with More slot. 7) Telemetry events emitted for slot clicks, expansions and predictive suggestions (spec provided to eng).
design_notes:
Iteration history: V1 used a dense icon rail; tests showed discoverability drop for occasional users. V2 introduced chip + icon pattern; users liked visual cues but found it heavy. V3 (this prototype) moves to slot cards with compact summary and micro-badges.

Trade-offs discussed:
- Complexity vs. discoverability: predictive ranking adds surface complexity but reduces long-term friction; fallback is a deterministic recency sort.
- Telemetry load: client-side ranking reduces server cost but requires careful sync when roles change.
- Rollout fidelity: micro-dashboard intentionally limited to 24h summary to avoid creating a full dashboard dependency inside the sidebar.

Open design questions for review:
- Should cost lens show absolute dollars or token counts by default? (PM prefers token counts for infra-savvy customers; finance has requested dollars for procurement teams.)
- Default slot order for new tenants: frequency-first or workspace-first?
- How to represent multi-tenant role contexts when a user has many cross-workspace roles?
decisions: 1) Use token counts as default metric with an optional toggle to show USD in flyout (decided 2026-03-03 after PM/Finance call). 2) Predictive ranking lives on the client using session hints; a server-side scoring API will be provided for enterprise-only telemetry sync (decision 2026-03-06). 3) 'More' overflow slot used instead of horizontal scrolling (decision 2026-03-07).
tradeoffs:
- Client ranking reduces network requests but requires local storage invalidation when permissions change.
- Showing rollouts inline improves visibility but risks information density; we capped the micro-dashboard to 3 KPIs.
- Adding cost badges increases visual noise; introduced a low-contrast baseline and hover for details to mitigate.
updates: 2026-03-02: Usability test with 6 participants (3 power, 3 occasional). Key feedback: quick-jump badges were useful; cost flyout needed clearer labeling.
2026-03-03: PM decision to default to token counts; added toggle for USD in micro-dashboard.
2026-03-06: Eng feasibility review: suggested client ranking with optional server sync for enterprise. Added telemetry event names to spec.
2026-03-08: Accessibility pass: ensured ARIA roles for slots and added screen reader copy for rollout stages.
2026-03-10: Design handoff package uploaded to Figma and Confluence; request for Eng PR review and scheduling for a gated beta.
notes_for_engineering: See 'Telemetry spec' link for event names. Implementation should prefer CSS-only collapse where possible for perf. Micro-dashboard data should be fetched lazily on first expansion. Provide feature-flag gating for predictive ranking and cost badges. Ensure progressive enhancement for older browsers.
